anomalies.observed: SW6 is a 2-pole DIP switch used with the two 120R CAN termination resistors, but the CAN0 termination node is tied to SW6.1 while /CAN0_P is tied to SW6.4, and the CAN1 termination node is tied to SW6.2 while /CAN1_P is tied to SW6.3. With the standard 2-bit DIP-switch pole pairing implied by the KiCad/DSHP02TS style used here (1-3 and 2-4, analogous to SW7's 1-5/2-6/3-7/4-8 usage), closing SW6 cross-couples /CAN0_N to /CAN1_P and /CAN1_N to /CAN0_P instead of terminating each bus to its own CAN_P line.
anomalies.expected: Each independent CAN bus should be terminated only within itself: R34 should switch /CAN0_N to /CAN0_P, and R35 should switch /CAN1_N to /CAN1_P. CAN0 and CAN1 are described as separate buses and should not be cross-coupled by the termination switch.

evidence.quote: SW6 | SW_DIP_x02 | Button_Switch_SMD:SW_DIP_SPSTx02_Slide_KingTek_DSHP02TS_W7.62mm_P1.27mm | Switch:SW_DIP_x02 | 2x DIP Switch, Single Pole Single Throw (SPST) switch, small symbol

anomalies.impact: If the termination switch is enabled, the two independent CAN buses are cross-coupled and improperly terminated. This can load both buses, distort CAN differential levels, and cause CAN communication errors or loss of communication with the motor controllers.

anomalies.observed: The net named /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of three LEDs (D4, D14, D23). It is not connected to +3V3, 3.3V_PI_OUT, or any other 3.3 V source or driver.
anomalies.expected: A net named as a 3.3 V LED power net should be connected to a current-limited 3.3 V supply, or to a driver that can source current, so that the status LEDs can illuminate when their cathode-side sinks are active.
anomalies.impact: D4, D14, and D23 will not light because their anodes are floating. This changes the intended visual status behavior of the board even though the CM4 GPIO/Ethernet LED outputs may be operating correctly.

parsed.summary: The build shows at least one likely serious connectivity anomaly: the CAN termination switch SW6 is wired so that enabling it cross-couples the two independent CAN buses instead of terminating each bus separately. A second supported issue is that the /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW net is left as a floating LED-anode net with no 3.3 V source connection.
